A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. Matching relocated sections, original plots, and case studies supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original math-benchmark evaluations, CoT verification results, and training-dynamics measurements from the authors' DAPO reproduction.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds original LiveCodeBench evaluations, distilled-model comparisons, and supervised fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: The GRPO/DAPO procedure, answer-based reward, CoT-Pass@K definition, verifier prompt, and verification aggregation remain unchanged. SFT is introduced as an experimental probe of CoT quality, rather than a modification to the RL method.

E1.justification: v2 adds competitive code generation evaluated through execution on LiveCodeBench versions v1–v6. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's mathematical-reasoning benchmarks. The five original math benchmarks and DAPO training questions are retained.

E2.justification: The Qwen2.5-32B versus DAPO comparison is retained. v2 additionally compares DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B with AceReason-Nemotron-7B, Skywork-OR1-7B, and Skywork-OR1-Math-7B in the relevant experiments, and introduces SFT-trained comparison models in Figure 6.

E3.justification: Added protocols include execution-based coding evaluation, LiveCodeBench difficulty subsets, and controlled SFT experiments starting from the same Qwen2.5-32B model with CoTs from different RL stages and correctness groups. These substantially expand the evaluation design; the original mathematical metrics and verification procedure are retained.

E4.justification: New Section 6 tests CoT quality through downstream SFT generalization, varying the generating checkpoint and using correct, incorrect, or all CoTs. Appendix A.4 adds difficulty-specific coding analysis identifying which problems sustain high-K gaps. The original manual case studies are retained as Appendix A.8.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three CoT verifications and the same voting strategies. New Figure 6(a) contains box-and-whisker marks for SFT performance, but their meaning and source of variation are unspecified. Consequently, whether they introduce a new uncertainty-estimation or repeated-run practice cannot be established reliably.

E6.justification: v2 adds coding Pass@K advantages in Figures 3 and 8, the absence of a distinct high-K advantage for the distilled-model AIME comparison in Figure 9, and improving SFT generalization with later-stage CoTs in Figure 6. The original benchmark and training plots are retained, so these are added findings rather than revised scores for the original comparisons.

T1.justification: The alpha > beta assumption, expected-advantage theorem, proof, variance and ideal-case derivations, and metric definitions are retained. Much of v1 Section 3 moves to v2 Section 4 and Appendix A.5; renaming Logical Coherence to Logic Prior does not change the assumption.

C1.justification: The central claim that RLVR incentivizes correct reasoning remains, but v2 explicitly claims demonstrated reasoning-boundary extension in both math and coding. Its introduction and conclusion also add SFT replication of post-RLVR capabilities from generated CoTs as a principal contribution, absent from v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for the contrasting effects of RLVR on distilled models in math and coding, and interprets the SFT results as evidence that even imperfect later-stage CoTs improve in quality. It explicitly connects DAPO reward saturation to an inability to correct remaining reasoning errors. The earlier response-length and overthinking explanation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds an official LiveCodeBench evaluation-repository pointer and describes the SFT base model, training-question source, and answer filtering. Existing hardware, training duration, data sources, and verifier prompt are retained, largely through relocation. Detailed SFT hyperparameters are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 positions its coding experiments as reproducing and extending AceReason results and comparing Skywork. It removes the long-CoT survey by Qiguang Chen and works by Jiang, Ouyang, and Yan from the bibliography. Most research positioning remains; AceReason's changed citation-year suffix does not denote a new reference.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Empirical evaluation now precedes theory, while proofs, discussions, and much training detail move into the appendices. The verifier appendices are merged, case studies are renumbered, and author ordering changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds coding, SFT, and distilled-model comparison figures and substantially rearranges figure placement and surrounding layout. Original plots are retained: notably, v1 Figure 3(a) is redisplayed as v2 Figure 4, while the complete original training figure remains as Figure 10.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support concentrated on one 32B math-model comparison and judge-assessed reasoning. v2 substantially strengthens that foundation through execution-checked coding evaluations and SFT transfer experiments, while the distilled-model math results usefully qualify applicability. These additions address important limitations of the original evidence. Incomplete SFT implementation details and unexplained spread markers limit reproducibility, but do not outweigh the broader and more varied support for the central argument.
